function_1: fertilization component with mixed pollination/selfing attribution
eligibility_reason: Fertilization and nonpredation are both related to stalk height, but fertilization is not a pure pollinator-mediated component because selfing can contribute strongly, so fixed pollinator-vs-predator geometry is not identified.
notes: Both fertilization and nonpredation show largely consistent disruptive selection across populations; this is not promoted to pollinator–seed-predator conflict.

plant_taxon: multiple Costa Rican cloud-forest plant species
trait_coordinate: flowering display across disturbance patch types
eligibility_reason: The study compares patch types and plant–hummingbird interactions; it does not estimate two functional responses to one declared plant trait axis.
notes: Relative nectar piercing versus legitimate visits changes in large gaps, but this is a context effect rather than a same-trait functional geometry.

eligibility_reason: Floral odor, visitor preference and seed-predation/fertilization ratios covary with elevation, but seed-predator response to the same odor coordinate is not identified.
source_basis: Carvajal Acosta et al. 2023 Ecology and Evolution DOI 10.1002/ece3.10418
notes: The damaged-to-fertilized seed ratio rises with elevation, but this is not an odor-specific antagonist response.

eligibility_reason: The same bumblebee species is the primary pollinator and also robs nectar; flower height predicts robbery, but a fixed mutualist-versus-antagonist sign is biologically inappropriate.
source_basis: Du et al. 2015 Biodiversity Science DOI 10.17520/biods.2015102
notes: Robbing does not reduce fruit set, seed number or seed mass; robbed flowers show more stigmatic closure and are taller.

eligibility_reason: Taller flowering stems receive more pollination while shorter stems experience more seed predation, so both ecological routes favor greater height.
source_basis: Walsh et al. 2014 AoB PLANTS DOI 10.1093/aobpla/plu031
notes: This is reinforcement, not a pollinator–seed-predator conflict: greater height simultaneously increases pollination and reduces predation.

eligibility_reason: Floral display size predicts floral visitation, whereas degree of seed predation is associated with plant isolation rather than display size.
notes: Display size has a pollinator route but no matched seed-predator response on the same axis; reproductive success is dominated by isolation.

eligibility_reason: The spotted morph is preferred by the dominant efficient pollinator but suffers greater ovule predation by florivores.
source_basis: de Jager & Ellis 2013 Annals of Botany DOI 10.1093/aob/mct189
notes: Pollinator benefit and florivore cost oppose on one discrete floral signal coordinate; community composition varies among sites but component-specific context shifts remain to be quantified.
